title: Q2 Roadmap: Elastic Dedicated Pools & Autoscale Guardrails (operational slice)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver an operational Q2 slice that makes Dedicated pools elastic with guardrails that protect latency SLOs and committed economics. Scope includes: (1) a lightweight commitment-exchange window allowing customers to increase/decrease reserved capacity within a defined SLA window; (2) autoscale guardrails that apply per-customer policies (min pool size, burst caps, cooldowns); (3) telemetry surfaces and alerts in Console to show cost delta and request-level throttling; (4) rollout plan with canary traffic and fallbacks to hosted variants. Rationale: many mid-market customers report periodic spikes that blow committed pools or force manual ops. This initiative balances predictable unit economics with operational resilience by offering automated, observable elasticity rather than manual ticket-driven capacity changes. Trade-offs: conservative guardrails reduce overcommit risk but may delay immediate burst capacity for some workloads; we prioritize latency and cost predictability over pure burst throughput in this first slice.

okrs: OKR-Q2-Elasticity-01: Reduce manual capacity change tickets by 60% for pilot customers
OKR-Q2-Performance-02: Maintain p95 token latency within 1.25x of baseline under autoscale events
OKR-Q2-Cost-03: Keep per-token cost delta from autoscale < 10% above reserved baseline for 95% of requests
acceptance_criteria: Customers can request reservation adjustments via API and Console and receive kubernetes-like acknowledgement with ETA
Autoscale events obey per-customer guardrails (min, max, burst cap, cooldown) in 95% of test cases
Console shows cost delta, max pool usage, and autoscale event history for last 30 days
Two pilot customers validate behavior under real traffic and sign-off on latency and billing transparency

risks: Risk: Autoscale events could cause transient token latency increase due to KV cache repopulation. Mitigation: staged warm-up and traffic steering to warm instances first.
Risk: Billing transparency confusion for customers during autoscale. Mitigation: Console cost delta visualization and pre-commit simulation mode.
Risk: API-level race conditions when two change requests overlap. Mitigation: implement idempotent change tokens and a short serializing window at service layer.
